note: Canonical lessons ledger. One row per decision about something the estate learned, from either intake: the harvest names the venture, the Study workflow names the sources it read and the lens it read them through. Declines and deferrals stay as rows, because a decision that leaves no trace gets argued again. registry/LESSONS.md is the derived view of this file. Schema: kernel/schemas/lesson.schema.json.
preamble:
The lessons ledger. Two intakes write here: the harvest, which pulls
rulings and feedback from a governed venture, and the Study workflow,
which reads a named source through a lens contract. Every row carries
a disposition that points at the file which now owns the decision, and
a declined lesson keeps its reason, so a decline cannot be re-proposed
as if it had never been argued. A silent harvest month still records
"checked, clean".

Disposition is an enum. `kernel/schemas/lesson.schema.json` lists
the permitted values and refuses one that is not on the list, and
`TOUR.md` is the home for what they mean: its table under "The
eleven dispositions" defines all eleven. Each value names the kind
of home a decision found; the row's own `outcome` and `informs`
name the file that holds it now. The value `binding` is absent on
purpose: this ledger can propose a binding candidate and nothing
more, because binding needs an accepted ADR and the operator under the
ladder in `GOVERNANCE.md`.

**A lesson leaves this ledger once its content is stated as a rule
somewhere else.** Keeping it here as well would be a second home for
the same rule, and one of the two homes would go stale. Rows that
record what changed and why are provenance, and those stay.

The first PB-E02 harvest ran on 2026-08-08 against the three governed
ventures. Venture A's two entries had both already been folded during
the v1 build and are recorded as such below. Venture C's feedback file
carried fifteen entries and a matured stack profile, and is the
substance of this harvest. PatterTech_Website ships no feedback file:
it predates the template, which is itself a finding and is queued.

Earlier rows came from the estate survey at EOS creation and from the
Venture A reseed feedback.

The PB-E04 promotion review ran the same day and promoted nothing. The
sample: zero live `lifecycle: experimental` items, so nothing expired
past the ninety-day window; zero `lifecycle: contested` rules; the
twenty-four binding rules in `packs/` unchanged; and no exception
ledger to sample, because ADR-0004 withdrew `org/exceptions.jsonl` and
moved a one-off exception onto the task record it applies to. Of the
harvest's three promotion candidates, each carries one argued ruling
from one venture, which under the ladder in `GOVERNANCE.md` is short
of binding-candidate. Venture C's five draft wargames stay candidates
for the same reason: a fork that happened once is not a recurring fork,
and a guide written for it would be speculation with a filename.

rows.title: Hydration warnings are often browser-extension noise
rows.lesson: Hydration warnings are often browser-extension noise; verify in a clean profile before treating one as a bug.
rows.source_note: Recorded at EOS creation as "Lesson row only, declined as doctrine (too narrow)".
rows.outcome: Declined. No guide id and no evidence row, on purpose.
rows.applicability_conditions: Browser applications reporting hydration or client-render mismatches in development.
rows.reasoning: Too narrow to bind, and no pack owns it.

rows.title: Plan and build decouple, and nothing in the build is generative
rows.lesson: Plan and build decouple: agent-driven planning, a deterministic byte-stable build, nothing generative in the build step.
rows.source_note: Recorded at EOS creation against Venture D under the repository name it carried then, and corrected to its current name in the v2 pass on 2026-08-03.
rows.outcome: Became an EOS principle, "compiled, never composed", in `README.md`, and the compile contract in `kernel/README.md`.
rows.applicability_conditions: Any pipeline where an agent plans and a tool builds. What pays is a build a second run reproduces byte for byte.

rows.title: Stale docs are a bug, so delete them and ban-list the path
rows.lesson: Stale docs are a bug: delete them, ban-list the old path in a test, never archive in place.
rows.outcome: Absorbed into the supersession rules in `GOVERNANCE.md`.
rows.applicability_conditions: Repositories where documentation ships with the code and a superseded document keeps its old path.

rows.title: A design law one directory from the code may as well not exist
rows.lesson: A design law that lives one directory away from the code might as well not exist.
rows.outcome: WG-WEB-013 filed by the operator, now at `archive/v1-final:doctrine/web-design/wargames/WG-WEB-013-kit-escape-and-enforcement.md`, and carried into `packs/ui-ux/guides/GD-UIUX-004-token-source.md`.
rows.applicability_conditions: Products with a design system whose tokens are enforced somewhere other than the code that consumes them.

rows.title: Uniform ceremony kills small work
rows.lesson: Uniform ceremony kills small work; a bug fix must never need sixteen acceptance criteria.
rows.source_note: Recorded at EOS creation as "External (SDD research)", in the estate survey rather than from a venture. No evidence row was written for it at the time and none has been written since.
rows.outcome: Became the scale system and the WG-EOS-001 mandate, and then the whole of the v2 kernel: modes, tiers and ceremony budgets, ADR-0002.
rows.applicability_conditions: Any process applying one ceremony to work of different sizes. It stands on the practice that followed rather than on a cited source.

rows.title: Venture history in a template must be a slot, not boilerplate
rows.lesson: Template boilerplate that states venture history must be a slot; a reseed with real history should fill it, not overwrite it.
rows.outcome: Default changed: `kernel/templates/org/CONSTITUTION.tpl.md` gained the amendment-history slot.
rows.applicability_conditions: Compiling a template into a repository that already has history worth preserving.

rows.title: Dark-first loses to print-native institutional brands
rows.lesson: The dark-first surface register loses to print-native institutional brands; the ink-like clause carried a real venture.
rows.outcome: Argued ruling appended to WG-WEB-001, now at `archive/v1-final:doctrine/web-design/wargames/WG-WEB-001-surface-register.md`. One argued ruling from one venture, so it is not yet promotion evidence; the philosophy question it raises is carried by `packs/ui-ux/guides/GD-UIUX-001-design-philosophy.md`.
rows.applicability_conditions: Brands with a print-native or institutional register. One argued ruling from one venture, which under the ladder in GOVERNANCE.md is short of promotion evidence.

rows.title: Ancestry tables need preserved rows, not only compiled ones
rows.lesson: Reseeds meet pre-EOS files; the ancestry table needs normalised and preserved row kinds beyond compiled and authored.
rows.outcome: Default changed: `kernel/templates/COMPILE_REPORT.tpl.md` documents both kinds.
rows.applicability_conditions: Compiling into a repository that predates the template being compiled.

rows.title: A slot pattern that excludes digits lets a slot ship unfilled
rows.lesson: A slot pattern that excludes digits lets a digit-bearing slot ship unfilled through a green seed check.
rows.outcome: Bug fixed: E008's `SLOT_RE` in `tools/eos/checks/structural.py` widened to `[A-Z0-9_]+`, with a regression test. `{{SUCCESS_90}}` in `kernel/templates/VENTURE_BRIEF.tpl.md` was the live instance.
rows.applicability_conditions: Any checker matching template slots by pattern, where a slot name may carry digits.

rows.title: A checker that walks every file trips on vendored trees
rows.lesson: A checker that walks every markdown file under the seed path fails on vendored dependency trees.
rows.outcome: Already fixed in v2: `SKIP_DIRS` in `tools/eos/repo.py` skips `node_modules`, `.git`, `__pycache__` and `.pytest_cache`. Recorded as confirmation that the v2 rewrite closed it.
rows.applicability_conditions: Ventures whose repository carries vendored dependency trees under the seed path.

rows.title: A two-edit claim protocol lets two launchers collide
rows.lesson: A claim protocol where the queue row and the claim are two edits lets two launchers collide on one item.
rows.outcome: Fixed by design in v2: claims are coordinator-assigned and committed before dispatch, and lanes never acquire or mutate one (`kernel/schemas/claims.schema.json`).
rows.applicability_conditions: Any queue where more than one session can start work at the same time.

rows.title: Inception necessarily writes to main
rows.lesson: Inception necessarily writes to main, because the org that mandates branches is being compiled during the writes.
rows.outcome: Deferred at the harvest and queued as T-0005. That task closed on 2026-08-11: `inception/INCEPTION.md` states the Session 0 write-to-main exemption under its own heading, so the first review session no longer reads Session 0's history as a violation.
rows.applicability_conditions: Session 0 in a fresh venture repository, before the branch rule it is compiling exists.

rows.title: A cold-start probe finds defects a warm session cannot see
rows.lesson: A cold-start probe run before the human rubric is signed surfaces real defects a warm session cannot see.
rows.outcome: Promotion candidate for PB-E04. One argued ruling from one venture, so not yet binding evidence. The drill apparatus is the natural home: all twenty-two drills now carry scenarios and graders, and ADR-0007 defers running them, so nothing has graded this.
rows.applicability_conditions: A venture at Session 0 whose rubric is not yet signed, probed by a session with no prior context of the repository.

rows.title: Doctrine-heavy ventures walk long at Session 0
rows.lesson: A venture whose master prompt fixes deep product doctrine walks long at Session 0, because doctrine engages triggers the interview leaves silent.
rows.outcome: Deferred at the harvest and queued as T-0006. That task closed on 2026-08-11: `inception/WALK_ORDER.md` budgets interview-triggered and doctrine-triggered rulings separately, so a correct doctrine-heavy walk no longer reads as an overrun.
rows.applicability_conditions: Ventures arriving with fixed product doctrine already in the master prompt.

rows.title: Local-first PWA with a WASM core is a distinct proven shape
rows.lesson: A local-first browser product with a WASM compute core is a distinct proven shape, not a bend of the fullstack profile.
rows.outcome: Registry addition: `registry/stacks/STACK-local-first-pwa.md`, carrying S1's worked evidence and five sharp edges.
rows.applicability_conditions: A browser-delivered product whose data stays on the operator's machines and whose compute is latency-sensitive. Where the data may leave the machine, the fullstack profile is the cheaper shape.

rows.title: Platform-native deployment beats containers on a sovereign LAN
rows.lesson: Platform-native deployment beats the container default on a sovereign LAN with no parity or handover trigger.
rows.outcome: Contrary evidence recorded against the container default. Under `GOVERNANCE.md` precedence this triggers review, never automatic demotion, and one ruling from one venture is not promotion evidence. Carried to `packs/devops-reliability` at the next authoring pass.
rows.applicability_conditions: Deployment onto machines the operator owns, on a LAN, with no environment-parity requirement and no handover to another operator.

WG-OPS-002.note: The container default holds where environment parity or a handover to another operator is in play; this ruling covers a sovereign LAN with neither.

rows.title: A split voice register reads cleanly in practice
rows.lesson: A split voice register, warm-guide for in-app coaching and peer-expert for docs, reads cleanly in practice.
rows.outcome: Early supporting evidence for the three-way voice scope in `packs/writing-content/guides/GD-WRIT-003-voice-scope.md`, which already sanctions per-surface splits.
rows.applicability_conditions: Products carrying both in-app coaching copy and reference documentation, where one register would have to serve both.

rows.title: Cap urllib3 below 2.5 until a deploy proves otherwise
rows.lesson: urllib3 2.5 and above breaks Railway startup; cap it below 2.5.0 until a deploy proves otherwise.
rows.outcome: Now owned by `registry/stacks/STACK-fastapi-postgres.md`.
rows.applicability_conditions: Python services on the FastAPI and Postgres profile deploying to Railway.

rows.title: Dockerignore node_modules or Windows pnpm symlinks break the build
rows.lesson: Docker builds on Windows fail on pnpm symlinks unless every node_modules directory is dockerignored.
rows.outcome: Now owned by `registry/stacks/STACK-fullstack-app.md`.
rows.applicability_conditions: Docker builds run on a Windows host in a pnpm workspace.

rows.title: Generated artefacts need a drift check or they rot
rows.lesson: Generated artefacts, OpenAPI types and schemas among them, must be committed with a CI drift check, or they rot silently.
rows.outcome: Now owned by `packs/architecture/PACK.md` and its CHECKS row, argued in WG-ARCH-005.
rows.applicability_conditions: Any repository committing generated artefacts alongside the source they are generated from.

rows.title: Visual regression needs a pinned image or fonts diverge
rows.lesson: Visual regression needs a Docker-pinned image or fonts diverge across machines.
rows.outcome: Now owned by `packs/delivery-testing/PACK.md`, argued in WG-DEL-003.
rows.applicability_conditions: Test suites comparing rendered screenshots across machines.

rows.title: Migrations: forward-only, idempotent, advisory-locked
rows.lesson: Migrations: forward-only, idempotent, advisory-locked, run before app start, fail closed.
rows.outcome: Now owned by `packs/devops-reliability/guides/GD-DEVOPS-001-schema-change-strategy.md`.
rows.applicability_conditions: Relational schema changes shipped with the application that reads them.

rows.title: Ratcheting gates beat big-bang strictness
rows.lesson: Ratcheting gates, a mypy allowlist and coverage floors among them, beat big-bang strictness.
rows.outcome: Now owned by `packs/delivery-testing/refs/QUALITY_SIGNALS.md` and its CHECKS rows.
rows.applicability_conditions: Tightening quality gates on a codebase that does not pass them yet.

rows.title: The prune-and-fill compile is mechanical enough to script
rows.lesson: The prune-and-fill compile is mechanical enough to script; twenty lines compiled the two largest files with zero manual fixes.
rows.outcome: Now owned by `inception/INCEPTION.md` phase D.
rows.applicability_conditions: Compiling kernel templates into a venture repository where the fill values are already known.

rows.title: Local-first is seven ideals, and a product names the subset it buys
rows.lesson: Offline capability is one of the seven local-first ideals and not the load-bearing one: multi-device, collaboration, longevity, security and privacy, user control and no-spinners drive most of the architecture. A product that keeps its data on the operator's machines should name the subset it is buying and the ones it is declining, because shipped systems treat the list as a menu. A sync engine that narrowed itself to the read path and left writes to the application is the worked case: most of the benefit, a fraction of the cost.
rows.source_note: First worked instance of the Study workflow, written on 2026-08-10 during the v2.1 build over material already in the tree: the lens was recorded over the 2026-08-08 harvest and no new source was read. The reasoning line is this build's, not the operator's. LENS-0001 is the id reserved for the contract file, and on the day this row was decided no such file existed in this repository: the estate names no path for an EOS-side lens contract, and `kernel/templates/LENS.tpl.md` sends a venture's to `docs/lenses/`.
rows.outcome: Nothing changed. The row records the argument behind the shape already in `registry/stacks/STACK-local-first-pwa.md`, which was harvested at LES-0015 and states the shape without stating which ideals it buys.
rows.applicability_conditions: A local-first or browser-delivered product deciding how much sync to build. The primary source is a 2019 position paper by CRDT authors with a stake in the answer and no measurement behind it, so it argues the shape of the decision rather than settling it.
rows.reasoning: The profile already carried the shape; what it lacked was the argument for which ideals a machine-local product actually buys.
